answer: Admission requires a recorded lease on one harbor terrace cut into the seawall, plus a tagged lotus crate moored in the water directly below that plot. Twice a month a diver photographs the crate's barnacle map against the terrace number, and the pair is hashed. Any second crate under the same ledge, or a crate towed in from another berth, cancels the lease and docks the posted stake. Because ocean frontage is finite, a sybil swarm has to buy and occupy real terraces rather than mint cheap keys.
